AWPTCM-T33241.objective:
• The device can have a local loopback address assigned to it, and that address is shown in the device's interface and address information.
  • The loopback address can be reached from the device itself.
  • The loopback address stays reachable regardless of the state of the device's physical links.
  • The loopback address can be used as the source address for traffic the device sends.
  • An address that is not valid for a loopback interface is refused, and the existing configuration is left unchanged.
  • Removing the loopback address really does remove it, so it is no longer shown and can no longer be reached.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Assign a valid local loopback address to the device. Confirm the address appears in the device's interface and address information, and can be reached from the device itself.
Change the state of the device's physical links, including taking all of them down. Confirm the loopback address remains reachable from the device throughout.
Send traffic from the device using the loopback address as its source. Confirm the far end sees the loopback address as the sender.
Try to assign addresses that are not valid for a loopback interface. Confirm each one is refused and the existing configuration is unchanged.
Remove the loopback address. Confirm it is no longer shown in the interface and address information and can no longer be reached.
